claims.statement: X documents an access token secret (oauth_token_secret) issued together with the OAuth 1.0a user access token in the 3-legged flow.

sources.supports: access token secret by redirecting a user to X and having them authorize your application
sources.locator: Obtaining access tokens using 3-legged OAuth flow

sources.supports: * Access token secret === Token Secret === resulting `oauth_token_secret`

claims.statement: X states that the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret are different from the OAuth 1.0a consumer key and secret, and that an OAuth 1.0a access token and its token secret are exchanged together for OAuth 2.0 tokens.

sources.supports: These are different from your OAuth 1.0a consumer key and secret.
For each user, the access token and its token secret, as issued when the user authorized your app.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Format of the OAuth 1.0a access token secret is not stated on the pages read.
Whether the access token and its secret are one family or two for detection purposes is not settled by the pages; they are recorded as two candidates because the pages name them separately.
The candidate is established to exist from the pages read; its format (prefix, alphabet, length) is not researched.

Lead only: the Gitleaks twitter-access-secret rule (config/gitleaks.toml lines 3130-3133) captures 45 alphanumeric characters. No second maintainer was found with a corresponding artifact in the files read, so it stays unresolved.
